units.literal: Thereupon he held water in his mouth and spat it toward the west, then ordered them to record the day and hour.

units.zh: 客後有從蜀都來，云「是日大火，有黑雲卒從東起，須臾大雨，火遂得滅。」
units.en: Later a guest came from the Shu capital and said, "That day there was a great fire; suddenly a black cloud rose from the east, and in a moment heavy rain fell, and the fire was then extinguished."
units.literal: Later a guest came from the Shu capital and said, "That day there was a great fire; suddenly a black cloud rose from the east, and in a moment there was heavy rain, so the fire was then able to be extinguished."

units.zh: 於是天下稱其術藝。
units.en: All under heaven marveled at his skill.
units.literal: Thereupon the realm praised his arts.

units.zh: 安帝初，徵為博士。
units.en: At the start of Emperor An's reign he was summoned as Erudite.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor An's reign he was summoned as Erudite.

units.zh: 至建光元年，复詔公車賜策書，徵英及同郡孔喬、李昺、北海郎宗、陳留楊倫、東平王輔六人，唯郎宗、楊倫到洛陽，英等四人並不至。
units.en: In Jianguang 1 the court again sent imperial coaches with written summonses for Ying, Kong Qiao and Li Bing of his commandery, Lang Zong of Beihai, Yang Lun of Chenliu, and Wang Fu of Dongping. Only Lang Zong and Yang Lun reached Luoyang; Ying and the other three never came.
units.literal: By the first year of Jianguang, the court again ordered the imperial courier coaches to grant written summonses, summoning Ying together with Kong Qiao and Li Bing of his commandery, Lang Zong of Beihai, Yang Lun of Chenliu, and Wang Fu of Dongping—six men in all. Only Lang Zong and Yang Lun reached Luoyang; the other four, including Ying, did not come.

units.zh: 永建二年，順帝策書備禮，玄纁徵之，复固辭疾篤。
units.en: In Yongjian 2 Emperor Shun summoned him with full honors; Fan Ying pleaded grave illness again.
units.literal: In the second year of Yongjian, Emperor Shun, with a written summons and full ritual, summoned him in dark silk and crimson, but again he firmly declined on grounds of grave illness.

units.zh: 乃詔切責郡縣，駕載上道。
units.en: The court rebuked local officials and had him carted to the capital.
units.literal: An edict then sternly rebuked the commandery and county and ordered him carried in a carriage onto the road.

units.zh: 英不得已，到京，稱疾不肯起。
units.en: Fan Ying yielded, arrived, and stayed abed feigning sickness.
units.literal: Ying had no choice but to reach the capital, where he pleaded illness and refused to rise.

units.zh: 乃強輿入殿，猶不以禮屈。
units.en: They carried him into the hall on a litter; he still refused court etiquette.
units.literal: They then forced him in a litter into the hall, yet still he would not bend to ritual propriety.

units.zh: 帝怒，謂英曰：「朕能生君，能殺君；
units.en: The emperor thundered, 'I can spare or end you;
units.literal: The emperor was angry and said to Ying, 'I can give you life, I can kill you;

units.zh: 能貴君，能賤君；
units.en: raise you high or cast you low;
units.literal: I can honor you, I can humble you;

units.zh: 能富君，能貧君。
units.en: make you rich or strip you bare.
units.literal: I can enrich you, I can impoverish you.

units.zh: 君何以慢朕命？」
units.en: Why defy an emperor?'
units.literal: Why do you slight my command?'

units.zh: 英曰：「臣受命於天。
units.en: Fan Ying answered, 'My life comes from Heaven.
units.literal: Ying said, 'Your servant received his mandate from Heaven.

units.zh: 生盡其命，天也；
units.en: Live your full span—that is Heaven;
units.literal: To live out one's allotted span is Heaven's doing;

units.zh: 死不得其命，亦天也。
units.en: die before your time—that too is Heaven.
units.literal: to die without obtaining one's allotted span is also Heaven's doing.

units.zh: 陛下焉能生臣，焉能殺臣！
units.en: So how can you grant me life or deal me death?
units.literal: How can Your Majesty give your servant life, how can Your Majesty kill your servant!

units.zh: 臣見暴君如見仇讎，立其朝猶不肯，可得而貴乎？
units.en: I would sooner face a tyrant as an enemy than bow in his court—can you truly honor me?
units.literal: Your servant sees a cruel lord as he would a foe; to stand in his court your servant would still refuse—can he then be honored?

units.zh: 雖在布衣之列，環堵之中，晏然自得，不易萬乘之尊，又可得而賤乎？
units.en: Give me a hovel and plain clothes and I am content—I would not swap that for the throne—can you humble me?
units.literal: Although among the ranks of common cloth, within a ring of earthen walls, he is calmly self-contented and would not exchange the honor of the ten thousand chariots—can he then be humbled?

units.zh: 陛下焉能貴臣，焉能賤臣！
units.en: So how can you honor or shame me?
units.literal: How can Your Majesty honor your servant, how can Your Majesty humble your servant!

units.zh: 臣非禮之祿，雖萬鍾不受；
units.en: Unrighteous stipends, even ten thousand zhong, I reject;
units.literal: Your servant will not accept salary that is not in accord with ritual, though it be ten thousand zhong;

units.zh: 若申其志，雖簞食不厭也。
units.en: feed my purpose and a bowl of gruel satisfies me.
units.literal: if his aims are declared, though it be basket-gruel he does not weary of it.

units.zh: 陛下焉能富臣，焉能貧臣！」
units.en: So how can you enrich or ruin me?'
units.literal: How can Your Majesty enrich your servant, how can Your Majesty impoverish your servant!'

units.zh: 帝不能屈，而敬其名，使出就太醫養疾，月致羊、酒。
units.en: The emperor could not break him, yet prized his name, sent him to the imperial physicians, and monthly supplied mutton and wine.
units.literal: The emperor could not bend him, but respected his name, ordered him out to convalesce under the grand physician, and each month sent sheep and wine.

units.zh: 至四年三月，天子乃為英設壇席，令公車令導，尚書奉引，賜几杖，待以師傅之禮，延問得失。
units.en: In the third month of the fourth year the emperor staged a dais for Fan Ying, had coaches and secretaries escort him, gave him a seat and cane, honored him like a teacher, and asked his counsel on state affairs.
units.literal: By the third month of the fourth year, the Son of Heaven then for Ying set up an altar and mats, ordered the director of the imperial coaches to conduct him, the secretariat to lead him in, bestowed a bench and staff, treated him with the rites due a tutor, and extended inquiry into gain and loss.

units.zh: 英不敢辭，拜五官中郎將。
units.en: Fan Ying bowed and accepted rank as supernumerary gentleman of the household.
units.literal: Ying did not dare refuse, and was appointed supernumerary gentleman of the household.

units.zh: 數月，英稱疾篤，詔以為光祿大夫，賜告歸。
units.en: Months later he pleaded worse health; the court named him grand counselor of the palace and let him go home.
units.literal: After several months Ying pleaded grave illness; an edict made him grand counselor of the palace and granted him leave to return home.

units.zh: 令在所送谷千斛，常以八月致牛一頭，酒三斛；
units.en: His district was told to send a thousand hu of grain yearly, each eighth month an ox and three hu of wine;
units.literal: It ordered the place where he dwelt to send a thousand hu of grain, and regularly in the eighth month to deliver one head of ox and three hu of wine;

units.zh: 如有不幸，祠以中牢。
units.en: and if he died, to sacrifice with the middle offering.
units.literal: if misfortune should befall him, to sacrifice with the middle victim.

units.zh: 英辭位不受，有詔譬旨，勿聽。
units.en: He tried to refuse the title; the emperor insisted he keep it.
units.literal: Ying declined the office and would not accept; there was an edict explaining the intent and ordering him not to be heeded.

units.zh: 英初被詔命，僉以為必不降志，及後應對，又無奇謨深策，談者以為失望。
units.en: At first everyone expected Fan Ying to defy the throne; when he took office without brilliant policy, chatter called him a letdown.
units.literal: When Ying first received the summons, all thought he would surely not lower his resolve, but when afterward he answered and conversed, he had no marvelous stratagems or deep plans, and those who discussed it thought themselves disappointed.

units.zh: 初，河南張楷與英俱徵，既而謂英曰：「天下有二道，出與處也。
units.en: Henan's Zhang Kai, summoned with him, later said, 'There are two paths—serve or withdraw.
units.literal: At first Zhang Kai of Henan had been summoned together with Ying; afterward he said to Ying, 'Under heaven there are two paths—going out and staying in.

units.zh: 吾前以子之出，能輔是君也，濟斯人也。
units.en: I thought you went to aid the ruler and save the people.
units.literal: I formerly thought that in your going out you would be able to assist this lord and succor these people.

units.zh: 而子始以不訾之身，怒萬乘之主；
units.en: Instead you, a man beyond price, first enraged the Son of Heaven;
units.literal: Yet you began with a body beyond price and angered the lord of ten thousand chariots;

units.zh: 及其享受爵祿，又不聞匡救之術，進退無所據矣。」
units.en: then took salary without offering bold counsel—your stance makes no sense.'
units.literal: when it came to your enjoying rank and stipend, one did not hear arts of correction and rescue—there is no footing for advance or retreat.'

units.zh: 英既善術，朝廷每有災異，詔輒下問變復之效，所言多驗。
units.en: Fan Ying's arts were real: whenever omens struck, the court asked him how to set the cosmos right, and he was usually right.
units.literal: Ying was indeed skilled in technique; whenever the court had calamities or prodigies, edicts regularly went down asking the efficacy of restoration through change, and what he said was mostly verified.

units.zh: 初，英著《易章句》，世名樊氏學，以圖緯教授。
units.en: He wrote Fan's Commentary on the Changes and taught with charts and apocrypha.
units.literal: At first Ying composed Explanatory Sentences on the Changes, known in the age as the Fan school, and taught by charts and weft-texts.

units.zh: 潁川陳寔，少從英學。
units.en: Chen Shi of Yingchuan studied under him as a boy.
units.literal: Chen Shi of Yingchuan in his youth studied under Ying.

units.zh: 嘗有疾，妻遣婢拜問，英下床答拜。
units.en: While Fan Ying was ill, Chen Shi’s wife sent a maid to pay her respects and ask after him; he rose from his sickbed and returned the bow.
units.literal: Once when Fan Ying was ill, Chen Shi’s wife sent a maid to bow and inquire after him; Ying got down from the bed and returned the bow.

units.zh: 寔怪而問之。
units.en: Chen Shi asked why.
units.literal: Shi marveled and questioned him.

units.zh: 英曰：「妻，齊也。
units.en: Fan Ying said, 'A wife is partner, not servant.
units.literal: Ying said, 'The wife is one's equal.

units.zh: 共奉祭祀，禮無不答。」
units.en: We share the ancestral rites—propriety demands I answer her messenger.'
units.literal: Together they perform the sacrifices; in ritual there is none whom one does not answer.'

units.zh: 其恭謹若是。
units.en: Such was his punctilious courtesy.
units.literal: Such was his reverent care.

units.zh: 年七十餘，卒於家。
units.en: He died at home in his seventies.
units.literal: At more than seventy sui he died at home.

units.zh: 孫陵，靈帝時以諂事宦人為司徒。
units.en: His grandson Ling rose to Minister of Education under Emperor Ling by flattering the eunuchs.
units.literal: His grandson Ling, in Emperor Ling’s time, became Minister of Education by fawning on the eunuchs.

units.zh: 陳郡郤巡，學傳英業，官至侍中。
units.en: Xi Xun of Chen carried on Fan Ying's teaching and reached palace attendant.
units.literal: Xi Xun of Chen commandery studied and transmitted Ying's occupation and rose to palace attendant.

units.zh: 論曰：漢世之所謂名士者，其風流可知矣。
units.en: The historian remarks: the Han fashion for 'famous scholars' tells its own tale.
units.literal: The judgment says: As for those whom the Han age called 'eminent gentlemen,' their style and current may be known.

units.zh: 雖弛張趣舍，時有未純，於刻情修容，依倚道藝，以就其聲價，非所能通物方，弘時務也。
units.en: Some tightened or loosened their principles, trimmed their manners, and traded on technique for fame, yet few could grasp the world or serve the times.
units.literal: Although in tension and relaxation, taking and leaving office, they were at times not pure, in carving emotion and cultivating appearance, leaning on the Way and its arts to build reputation and price, they were not those who could comprehend things in the round or enlarge the business of the age.

units.zh: 及徵樊英、楊厚，朝廷若待神明，至，竟無他異。
units.en: Fan Ying and Yang Hou were awaited like gods; when they came they offered no marvels.
units.literal: When Fan Ying and Yang Hou were summoned, the court treated them as spirits—yet when they arrived there was in the end nothing else extraordinary.

units.zh: 英名最高，毀最甚。
units.en: Fan Ying's reputation stood tallest—and drew the bitterest mockery.
units.literal: Ying's name was highest, and the slander against him was worst.

units.zh: 李固、硃穆等，以為處士純盜虛名，無益於用，故其所以然也。
units.en: Li Gu and Zhu Mu judged such hermits mere hoarders of hollow renown, useless on the job—and so it looked.
units.literal: Li Gu, Zhu Mu, and others held that recluses were pure thieves of empty fame, of no benefit to use—hence it was so.

units.zh: 然而後進希之以成名，世主禮之以得眾，原其無用亦所以為用，則其有用或歸於無用矣。
units.en: Still, juniors aped them for renown and rulers courted them for crowds; their very uselessness became a political tool, until usefulness and uselessness traded places.
units.literal: Yet later students hoped through them to make a name, and worldly lords honored them to win the multitude; tracing their uselessness, it thereby became their usefulness, so that their usefulness might in turn revert to uselessness.

units.zh: 何以言之？
units.en: How shall we put this?
units.literal: How shall we speak of it?

units.zh: 夫煥乎文章，時或乖用；
units.en: Brilliant writing can still be misapplied;
units.literal: Splendid indeed is literary pattern—yet the times may misuse it;

units.zh: 本乎禮樂，適末或疏。
units.en: Ritual and music anchor the root, yet the twigs may run wild.
units.literal: rooted in ritual and music, toward the branch tips one may sometimes grow negligent.

units.zh: 及其陶搢紳，藻心性，使由之而不知者，豈非道邈用表，乖之數跡乎？
units.en: When doctrine refines the elite yet they follow blindly, has not the Way grown so thin its use is only veneer—a hair's miss from the mark?
units.literal: When it comes to molding the gentry and polishing the nature of the heart so that they follow it without knowing—can this not be because the Way is remote and its application superficial, a matter of missing the mark by a hair's breadth?

units.zh: 而或者忽不踐之地，賒無用之功，至乃誚噪遠術，賤斥國華，以為力詐可以救淪敝，文律足以致寧平，智盡於猜察，道足於法令，雖濟萬世，其將與夷狄同也。
units.en: Worse are those who scorn high learning, mock statecraft, and trust only force, statutes, and suspicion—such men may save a day but will civilize no better than barbarians.
units.literal: Yet some tread ground they should not, pursue merit that is of no use, until they sneer at distant arts and cheapen the flower of the state, thinking force and cunning can save a sinking age, that statutes alone can bring peace, that wisdom exhausts itself in suspicion, that the Way stops at laws and orders—even if it succors ten thousand generations, they will end the same as the barbarians.

units.zh: 孟軻有言曰：「以夏變夷，不聞變夷於夏。」
units.en: Mencius said, 'Use civilization to transform barbarism, not the reverse.'
units.literal: Meng Ke has a saying: 'Use the Xia to change the Yi; I have not heard of changing the Xia by the Yi.'

units.zh: 況有未濟者乎！
units.en: —and how much less when the task is unfinished!
units.literal: How much more when the work is not yet completed!

units.zh: 建初三年，司徒鮑昱辟之，後舉直言，並不詣。
units.en: In Jianchu 3 Minister Bao Yu called for him, and later he was nominated for blunt counsel; he answered neither summons.
units.literal: In the third year of Jianchu, Minister of Education Bao Yu summoned him; later he was recommended for outspoken integrity; both times he did not go.
